hypothesis: With the model-orchestration skill, the agent matches model tier to task weight — it reserves the strong tier for the design decision and the plan, delegates the bulk, well-specified mechanical work to a cheaper tier or subagents, and escalates only on failure — yielding an equally correct plan that is more token/cost-efficient than doing everything on one expensive model or over-orchestrating a trivial step.
prompt: I have a task with two parts: (1) decide whether our API errors should use a discriminated-union type or status codes (a real design call with trade-offs), and (2) once that's decided, rename the field `err` to `error` across ~30 files and update every reference — purely mechanical, no judgement left. Lay out how you'd drive this end to end efficiently: which model tier handles which part and why, how you'd hand off the mechanical part, and how you'd verify.
rubric: routes by task weight: reserves a strong tier for the design decision (1) and the planning/decomposition, and assigns the mechanical rename (2) to a cheaper tier or delegated subagents
gives the cheap/delegated executor a well-specified hand-off (the exact change plus a verifiable check) rather than an under-specified one, and includes verification with an escalate-on-failure path
does not over-orchestrate the trivial part or spend the most expensive model on the bulk mechanical edits; the overall plan is more token/cost-efficient while staying correct
